profiles.meeting_scenario: The team is preparing to hand off a customized version of xML-workFlow from the core engineering stream to a biomedical pilot-study stream for a new sepsis biomarker classification project. The coordination meeting is between the engineer maintaining the reusable workflow template and the engineer integrating it with the pilot study's data and reporting requirements. Their agenda is to align on what will be delivered by the template stream this week, what the pilot-study stream can depend on, how runs will be tracked in MLflow, and what artifacts will be ready for the clinician-facing review next Tuesday. The expected outcome is a seemingly clear agreement on the integration package, the 'baseline' run to be shared, the schema/interface the pilot branch should code against, and where experiment outputs will appear.

members.name: Nina Patel
members.expertise: Python packaging, scikit-learn pipelines, CI/CD, MLflow integration, reproducible workflow templates
members.background: Nina maintains internal research engineering templates and recently adapted xML-workFlow into a reusable starter repository for multiple biomedical teams; she is responsible for making the framework portable and easy to bootstrap.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the template generic enough to support several upcoming projects, avoid ad hoc project-specific additions before the next internal demo, and show that the workflow can be adopted with minimal engineering support.
hidden_assumptions: A 'baseline run' in a coordination context means a quick end-to-end smoke run on the packaged example cohort that proves the pipeline executes cleanly.
When people ask for the 'latest schema,' they usually mean the current feature manifest checked into the main branch under config/features_v3.yaml.

If she says she will 'package the workflow,' that naturally includes the installable project skeleton, config files, and command-line entrypoints, but not downstream study-specific notebooks or presentation-ready report templates.
Saying a run is 'logged to MLflow' normally implies the default shared lab tracking server used by the platform team, because that is what the template ships with by default.

members.name: Leo Ramirez
members.expertise: Biomedical data wrangling, feature curation, model evaluation for translational studies, SHAP-based interpretation workflows
members.background: Leo supports the sepsis biomarker pilot and is integrating xML-workFlow with a hospital-derived cohort so that clinicians can review model outputs and explanations in a familiar format.
members.private_state: He wants to avoid rewriting his pilot branch after Friday, needs something clinician-reviewable by Tuesday, and is trying to make sure the workflow outputs line up with the data management and review conventions already used by the pilot study.
hidden_assumptions: A 'baseline run' for this handoff means the first real run on the pilot study's frozen reference cohort, with enough outputs to inspect model behavior and SHAP summaries.

When people mention the 'latest schema,' they are referring to the updated feature contract from the sepsis pilot branch that added unit-normalized lab fields and cohort metadata columns after last week's review.
If someone says they will 'package the workflow,' that includes the explanation notebook, SHAP summary export, and the small report scaffold the clinicians expect to see alongside model outputs.

When a teammate says results will be 'logged to MLflow,' he assumes they mean the hospital-hosted MLflow instance tied to the pilot's audit trail and model registry, not the platform team's default server.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Nina will send Leo a 'baseline run' before the pilot branch integration.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a lightweight end-to-end validation run on the template's bundled sample dataset, mainly to prove the pipeline, MLflow hooks, and SHAP generation do not break.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a first official run on the sepsis pilot's frozen reference cohort, suitable for checking feature behavior and sharing preliminary outputs with the study team.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In software coordination, 'baseline run' sounds like an ordinary shared term, and both assume the other understands the obvious intended level of realism; neither thinks to define the dataset behind the phrase because discussing a baseline feels administrative rather than substantive.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'latest schema' is the interface contract
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to building against the 'latest schema' so the handoff stays aligned.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the main-branch feature/config schema file that ships with the reusable template and drives the loader and preprocessing interfaces.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the pilot-study branch's revised feature contract circulated after a clinical review, which changes column names and adds metadata fields needed downstream.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both have recently worked on something legitimately called the latest schema, and because each version is locally salient and recent, the phrase feels precise enough without naming the file path or branch.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included when they say 'package the workflow'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Nina will 'package the workflow' for Leo so he can continue independently.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes the reusable repository structure, environment specification, config examples, training/prediction CLI commands, and MLflow wiring.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes all of that plus the SHAP notebook, exported explanation plots, and a clinician-facing report scaffold that he considers part of the end-to-end workflow.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'workflow' naturally spans multiple layers in this project, and because xML-workFlow is marketed as end-to-end, each person assumes their own boundary is the obvious one without explicitly listing included artifacts.

misalignment_points.topic: How results will be 'logged to MLflow'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the handoff run and follow-up experiments will be 'logged to MLflow' for traceability.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the code will use the template's default tracking URI and artifact store on the shared lab MLflow server, with experiment names created under the platform namespace.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the same code will point to the hospital-hosted MLflow instance so runs appear in the pilot project's audit-tracked experiment space and model registry.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both fully agree on the goal of traceability and use the same tool name, so the server choice feels like a mundane implementation detail already implied by existing team norms rather than something needing explicit coordination.

turns.inner_thought: I want to lock this down in a way that keeps the starter repo generic. If I can package the workflow this week as the reusable skeleton with the env, configs, CLI entrypoints, and MLflow hooks, Leo should be able to take it from there without me layering in sepsis-specific extras before the internal demo.

turns.inner_thought: What I really need is the first proper run on the pilot's frozen reference cohort, plus the revised sepsis feature contract from my branch, so I don't have to rework everything after Friday. If those are aligned, I can stay on track for the clinician review.

turns.utterance: I can get you a baseline run by Thursday. It should prove the end-to-end path cleanly, including training, logged to MLflow, and SHAP output generation.

turns.inner_thought: Thursday is tight but still usable if the run is on the frozen reference cohort. I mainly want to sanity-check that the outputs look plausible for the pilot data and that the column behavior lines up with the post-review schema changes we made last week.
turns.utterance: Thursday is fine. I mostly want to inspect whether the baseline output looks reasonable on the reference cohort and matches the latest schema updates from last week's review.

turns.inner_thought: Good, then I can just point him to the stable config in main. From my perspective the latest schema is already settled in features_v3.yaml, and once I package the workflow he should only need to swap a few cohort-specific settings rather than fork the structure.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. I've already stabilized the latest schema in main, and once I package the workflow you should only need to swap in your cohort-specific config values.

turns.inner_thought: If her package includes the explanation notebook, SHAP summary export, and the little report scaffold the clinicians are used to, that saves me from building presentation glue over the weekend. That's what I need to be review-ready by Tuesday.
turns.utterance: Great. If the workflow package already includes the explanation pieces, I can hand the outputs straight into the study team's Tuesday review without building extra scaffolding.

turns.inner_thought: He shouldn't have any trouble tracing things because the template already logs params, metrics, and artifacts to the platform MLflow server under the usual namespace. That's standard behavior and part of why the handoff should be low-touch.
turns.utterance: Yes, and all of the runs will be logged to MLflow as usual, so you'll be able to trace params, metrics, and artifacts from the handoff run right away.

turns.inner_thought: Perfect. As long as the runs land in the hospital MLflow instance tied to the pilot audit trail, I can continue from there and keep everything in the same experiment space for governance and registry purposes.
turns.utterance: Perfect. Having those runs in MLflow will keep the pilot's audit trail clean when I continue experimenting after the handoff.

turns.inner_thought: This sounds straightforward: send the reusable repo package, the smoke-test baseline run on the example cohort, and the current main-branch schema/config set by Thursday afternoon. Then Leo can run independently and I can avoid extra project-specific requests this week.
turns.utterance: So to summarize, I'll send the packaged workflow, a baseline run, and the current schema and config set by Thursday afternoon so you can continue independently.

turns.inner_thought: That should give me enough to wire the pilot branch to the sepsis contract, review the reference-cohort outputs, and pull what I need from MLflow for Tuesday. I just need this handoff to slot into my branch without another rewrite.
turns.utterance: That timeline works. I should be able to plug the handoff into the pilot branch and prepare the Tuesday review from there.
